subject: Prepay rebalance: settlement window orchestration & VAT evidence request
messages:
From: Lena Park <lena.park@acme-retail.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Richards <tom.richards@acme-retail.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Rebalance request + VAT evidence

Marcus —

We ran a refreshed forecast this morning and Q3 usage for our commerce vertical is skewing much more heavily to EU (UK + DE) than we originally anticipated. We have an active annual prepay with Redwood (RW-ACME-2027-Q3) and want to avoid mid-quarter shortfalls. Two asks:

1) Can Redwood shift ~25% of our US prepay pool to EU (GB + DE) immediately, and then rebalance monthly thereafter if needed?
2) We need VAT evidence on file for the UK and Germany so our accounts-payable team can process invoices without manual hold. Specifically: VAT registration certificates and a sample invoice that matches our PO requirements (invoice number format, remit fields).

Preferred settlement window for our finance team is 1st–5th of the month (we currently see 1st–3rd). If you need to propose a different window, tell us the operational tradeoffs.

PO: ACME-PO-8743 (please mirror on invoices).

Thanks — please loop in revenue ops and billing.

— Lena Park
Head of Finance, Acme Retail
Lena.Park@acme-retail.com
+1 415-555-0198

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Rebalance request + VAT evidence

Thanks Lena — got it. Appreciate the heads-up on the forecast. High level response and immediate next steps below.

Summary of proposed approach (we can execute within 48–72 hours once evidence is in):
- Option A (Immediate): One-time ledger reallocation of 25% from US pool into EU ledger this week; follow-up monthly reconciliations.
- Option B (Staged): Move 10% now, 10% at the start of next month, remaining 5% conditional on usage. Less operational change but slower safety margin.

Recommended settlement window: 1st–4th of the month (versus your 1st–5th ask). Moving to 1st–4th allows us to complete cross-border currency clearances without pushing invoices past AP batch deadlines; we can make an exception to 1st–5th if ACME requires it and signs off on slightly later posting.

What we need from Acme ASAP to action Option A:
- VAT registration certificates for each legal entity (GB, DE). A PDF or gov portal screenshot works.
- Confirmation that ACME wants us to use PO ACME-PO-8743 on the invoice line (you already confirmed but we need explicit attachment or one-line reply).
- Bank remit details for the EU ledger if payments will be wired to a different account than the US remit.

I’ve attached a proforma invoice sample and an invoice schema that shows the fields our billing system emits (invoice number format, currency, tax breakdown). If you can drop the VAT certs into the shared Drive link (or reply with attachments), Vanessa will pick this up and wire the change into the billing system.

Attachments: RW_proforma_invoice_sample.pdf; Requested_Invoice_Schema.xlsx

Marcus —

Thanks for the quick reply and the attachments. I uploaded the UK VAT certificate to your drive folder and attached the GB cert to this reply (Acme_VAT_Certificate_GB.pdf). Germany is still with our tax counsel — I expect to have DE cert by Monday.

We confirm ACME-PO-8743 should be on the invoice. Our AP team also asked for the invoice number to include the region code (example: INV-GB-20270601-0001) — the schema you sent looks okay, but can you confirm the regional tag will be inserted for EU invoices?

Tom from our payments team will be copied here on remit details once we confirm which bank (US vs EU) to use for settlement.

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@acme-retail.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Jun 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Operational runbook: prepay reallocation and settlement window change

Hi Lena / Marcus —

Thanks for uploading the GB VAT cert — received. Below is the ops runbook we will follow once we have the DE certificate and final remit account:

1) Authorization: Written confirmation from ACME (Lena / Tom) to proceed with Option A. Reply to this thread.
2) Ledger change (T+1 business day): Finance ops will create a ledger transfer for 25% of the US prepay balance into the EU ledger and tag entries with PO ACME-PO-8743.
3) Settlement window update (effective next cycle): Update billing cadence to 1st–4th (per Marcus recommendation). If ACME insists on 1st–5th, we will set 1st–5th for EU invoices only (to match local AP cadence) — confirm preference.
4) Invoice formatting: We will insert a region code in the invoice number (INV-GB-YYYYMMDD-####) for EU invoices; this matches the schema in Requested_Invoice_Schema.xlsx.
5) Reconciliation & thresholds: Reconciliation report will run on the 6th for the previous month; auto-top-up threshold set to $50,000. If usage > threshold, we will pull an emergency drawdown within the same settlement window and notify ACME.
6) Tax evidence retention: We will store VAT certs in the secure billing folder and surface the cert ID on invoice metadata.

Action items:
- ACME: Provide DE VAT cert and confirm remit account (Tom) — due Mon 21 Jun.
- Redwood (Vanessa): Schedule ledger transfer and update billing cadence — target Tue 22 Jun.
- Redwood (Marcus): Confirm final invoice sample and send to ACME treasury for sign-off — target Tue 22 Jun.

Links: HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/deal/12345) and billing folder (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C).

Vanessa Ortiz
Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com

All —
